title.en: Seeing Off Xin Jian at Lotus Tower

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource.

source.name: Wikisource
source.url: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/芙蓉樓送辛漸_(寒雨連江夜入吳)

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died around 757.
basis.zh: 唐诗，作者约卒于 757 年。

note.en: Wang Changling was serving in a minor post on the lower Yangtze when he sent this message north with a departing friend; Wikisource gives two poems under the title, and this is the first. The last line is his answer to anything people might say about him: his heart is as clear as ice in a jade vessel. It is a whole reputation, sent by word of mouth, in seven characters.
note.zh: 王昌龄任江宁丞时，托北归的朋友带回这句话；维基文库此题下有两首，这是第一首。最后一句是他对一切流言的回答：一片冰心在玉壶。一个人的清白，托人口头带回，只用了七个字。

excerpt.orig: 洛陽親友如相問，一片冰心在玉壺。
excerpt.en: If friends and family in Luoyang ask after me, / tell them: a heart of ice in a jade pot.
excerpt.zh: 洛阳亲友如相问，一片冰心在玉壶。

gloss.en: Wu, the old name for the lower Yangzi region. The Lotus Tower stood at Runzhou, present-day Zhenjiang.
gloss.zh: 吴：今江苏南部一带，古属吴地。芙蓉楼在润州（今江苏镇江）。

gloss.en: The hills of Chu. The land here had belonged to Wu and later to Chu, so the two names alternate.
gloss.zh: 楚山：楚地的山。镇江一带春秋属吴，战国属楚，故吴、楚可以互称。

gloss.en: Xin Jian was going north to Luoyang, where the poet had friends and family.
gloss.zh: 辛渐此行北上洛阳，作者的亲友在那里。

gloss.en: A heart as pure as ice in a jade pot: the image goes back to Bao Zhao, ‘straight as a red silk string, clear as ice in a jade pot’.
gloss.zh: 比喻心地纯洁。语出鲍照《代白头吟》“直如朱丝绳，清如玉壶冰”。
